A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Moner paper, with 22 complete, readable pages including Appendices A.1–A.4. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish matching scientific content; differences are confined to publication metadata.

before.justification: v3 reports original fastMRI and MoDL reconstruction and motion-estimation experiments, ablations, and runtime results in Section 4, plus simulated and real-world 3D MRI experiments in Appendix A.1.

after.justification: v4 retains the original benchmark, ablation, runtime, and simulated and real-world 3D MRI results in Section 4 and Appendix A.1.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical INR architecture, quasi-static motion estimation, projection-space optimization, and coarse-to-fine hash encoding. The 3D extension in Appendix A.1 is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same fastMRI and MoDL data under identical acceleration and motion scenarios, plus the same simulated 3D brain data and acquired 3D scans in Appendix A.1.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 7 retain NuIFFT, TV, DRN-DCMB, and Score-MoCo. Table 1 retains TV and Score-MoCo for motion accuracy, while Appendix A.1 retains NuIFFT for the 3D comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices A.1–A.3 retain identical splits, sampling and motion simulations, training budgets, scan-acquisition settings, image registration procedures, and reconstruction and motion metrics.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 contains the same motion-model, forward-model, and hash-encoding ablations, with identical supporting tables and figures. The appendix motion-trajectory and reconstruction analyses are also unchanged.

E5.justification: The existing mean/standard-deviation reporting and t-test significance annotations are identical. No run-count, seed, uncertainty-estimation, or statistical-testing information is added or removed.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain every numerical result and significance annotation. Runtime comparisons, reconstructed images, motion trajectories, and qualitative findings also match throughout the main text and appendices.

T1.justification: Equations 1–14 and their accompanying assumptions and reasoning are unchanged, including the Fourier-slice formulation, 2D and 3D motion transforms, and Appendix A.2 motion-error definitions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical contributions and claims about unsupervised motion correction, in-domain comparability, out-of-domain advantages, reconstruction quality, and efficiency.

C2.justification: Interpretations of domain generalization and frequency-dependent motion estimation are unchanged. Section 5 retains the same applicability limitations, and Appendix A.1 retains the same preliminary interpretation of real-world results.

D1.justification: Architecture details, hyperparameters, optimization schedules, hardware, scan parameters, metric libraries, baseline implementation notes, and code links are identical in Section 4.1 and Appendices A.1–A.3.

R1.justification: The cited works and bibliography are unchanged, as is the positioning relative to supervised motion correction, Score-MoCo, and prior INR reconstruction methods in Section 2 and elsewhere.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv margin stamp changes from v3 dated 6 February 2025 to v4 dated 15 July 2025. The title, authors, prose, terminology, section order, and appendix structure remain identical.

P2.justification: All 18 figures and seven tables retain identical displays, captions, formatting, and placement. Rendered pages 2–22 are pixel-identical; the first-page difference is confined to the arXiv stamp text.

improvement.justification: v4 preserves v3's scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, limitations, and reproducibility information, including all appendices. The updated arXiv stamp, PDF metadata, and added publication hyperlink do not materially change the paper's overall quality.
